current_alert.title: Abdul El-Sayed compares himself to JFK regarding questions about Muslim Brotherhood ties - WRGB

retrievals.source: exact Google News URL from the alert row
retrievals.finding: Google News shell only; no publisher URL/body/date.

retrievals.source: AOL syndicated article discovered by one exact-title search
retrievals.finding: AOL page says the post first appeared on Mediaite; provides full article text and its own canonical Mediaite URL. This is a syndicated copy, not direct Mediaite capture.

facts_attributed_by_article: The Mediaite article says El-Sayed answered an MS NOW interview question by comparing scrutiny of alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties to anti-Catholic loyalty questions faced by John F. Kennedy; he argued assumptions of dual loyalties were unfair and invoked religious freedom.

The article attributes family-tie claims to the sister’s reported 2012–2013 social-media posts, citing Washington Free Beacon; it also reports El-Sayed denied ties in an Oct 11 Meet the Press interview. These are reported allegations and candidate statements, not independent verification.

No separate direct MS NOW clip URL was present in the captured article text/links; the page says “Watch above via MS NOW.” Article makes only a generic statement about polling, without naming a poll, sample, method, field dates, or numerical result.

comparison.prior_title: Abdul El-Sayed compares himself to JFK regarding questions about Muslim Brotherhood ties - WKEF
comparison.prior_result: Same JFK-comparison headline was previously seen via WKEF; prior Google News resolution returned shell only and exact WKEF body remained unavailable. The title is near-identical, but source-body equality or a WRGB-to-Mediaite syndication link is not proved. The retrieved Mediaite/AOL text concerns an Oct17 MS NOW interview and adds no poll measurement; no basis here to claim a distinct new voter fact.

poll_context_from_prior_review.fact: Prior CBS Detroit coverage referenced Oct1 Mitchell likely-voter poll 45.6–41.4, MOE 3.8; this is previously reviewed context, not a new result in this alert.

limits: The original Mediaite page and WRGB page were not retrieved within the 3-attempt budget; AOL is a syndicated body that names Mediaite as original publisher.
No direct original candidate-response video URL was captured.
Title similarity does not prove the older WKEF alert and current WRGB alert carry byte-identical article bodies.
